attemptAccounting.note: These are the operator's numbers.  A dispatch and a spent attempt are counted separately here because they are not the same event: the production workflow has been dispatched three times, once refused inside the isolation before any output file existed and ruled unspent, and twice past the marker and therefore spent.  Every total in this block is the count of the rows in priorAttempts and can be re-derived from them.  This authority carries exactly one new attempt and nothing else.

boundInputDigests.note: Every file this authority depends on, in one table, so that drift is checked by iterating rather than by reading prose.  A digest here that no longer matches its file is an abort condition, not a note to update.  The records of the three prior dispatches are in this table for that reason: preserving them is a condition of this attempt, and a condition the production re-checks on the runner is worth more than one only a test reads.  The producing module and its gate are named in the producer fingerprint instead, because the module pins this authority's digest and a pin in both directions could not be written in either order.

boundaries: no wallet seed, passphrase or key derivation material is placed in or passed to the guest
no model API key is placed in or passed to the guest
no reward, block, consensus or peer-to-peer authority is granted to the guest
no network device and no shared directory is configured for the guest
no operator key, team identifier, certificate or provisioning profile is created
no public mining, no public testnet, no paid benchmark and no leaderboard claim

budgetBoundary.afterConsumption: no re-run, no retry and no second dispatch in this wave.  A consumed attempt that failed is reported to the operator as a hard stop.
budgetBoundary.changedFromTheSecondAuthority: The second authority drew the line at the first output file.  Two dispatches showed that line cannot be read after the fact: the first created the output directory and no file in it, and the operator had to rule on whether that counted.  The line is now a file the run writes on purpose, so the question is answered by looking rather than by reasoning.  This is narrower than the old rule, not wider -- everything that spent an attempt under the old wording still spends one under this one.
budgetBoundary.preflightNeverConsumes: the preflight cannot reach the section that writes the marker, and a test reads its call graph to say so.  No preflight outcome can consume the production budget.
budgetBoundary.rule: A refusal raised before ATTEMPT-CONSUMED.json exists does not consume the one allowed attempt.  Once that file has been written, the attempt is consumed whatever happens next -- including a failure, a crash, a cancelled job or a destroyed runner.
budgetBoundary.whyItIsDrawnThere: the marker is written before the first image file and is the only thing in the output directory whose presence means one specific thing.  It is written atomically, echoed to the console as it is written, and left world-readable so the step that collects it can, which is three independent ways for it to survive a job that dies.

expectedMeasurements.note: These are the numbers the sealed measurement recorded.  The preflight must reproduce the first set exactly; the production-bound set is what the same tree becomes once the launcher the runner rebuilds is staged into it.

hardStopConditions.note: The thirteen conditions carried over are carried over word for word: nine from the second authority and four from the third.  The four below are added, and adding is the only edit this list takes.  No inherited condition is reworded, reordered or dropped, and a test reads both earlier authorities to check that.

historicalPathLeftIntact.crossContaminationIsRefused: The predecessor path handed the successor lock, and the successor path handed the predecessor lock, must each refuse rather than build.  Neither direction may fall back to the other.

evidenceItReadsThePredecessorLock.note: build_oci_layout is called with no nested tree argument, so the runtime rootfs and its manifest cannot be in what it produces.

historicalPathLeftIntact.note: The predecessor production path is not edited, not re-pointed and not deleted.  It reads the v1 lock and imports the v1 builder, which is exactly what reproduces the image that already booted.  Keeping it runnable is what makes the earlier boot result still checkable.

limits.onExceeding: refuse.  Nothing is truncated, sampled or excluded to fit -- a tree that does not fit is the finding, and shrinking it to pass would hide it.

preflight.producedNothingIsCheckedAgainstTheDisk: The step that follows the run asks the filesystem whether any of the three output names or the consumed-attempt marker exists anywhere under the runner temporary tree, and fails if one does.  The four names are read out of the producer authority and the phase rather than written down again here.
preflight.purpose: Establish, without producing anything, that the successor path assembles exactly the tree the measurement sealed and that the three gaps are closed in the tree it actually assembles.
preflight.runsOn: the same arm64 Linux environment the production uses

uploadsItMay.why: The third authority wrote 'upload an artifact' in this list while the workflow uploaded its evidence document, which read as a contradiction between the rule and the run.  The rule was never about evidence: a small JSON document describing a run that produced nothing is the whole point of a repeatable preflight, and forbidding it would leave the cheap mode with nothing to show.  What is forbidden is an image artifact, and it is now named as one.

preflightResultStillStands.why: it measures the assembled tree, and every input that tree is built from is bound by digest in this authority at the same value the second one bound it at.  Nothing it measured changed, so it is not re-taken and not re-written; it records the digest of the authority it ran under, which is the second one, and that is correct.
preflightResultStillStands.yetANewPreflightRunsAnyway: the attempt still begins with a full preflight inside the production unit, because a sealed measurement is not a statement about this runner on this day

priorAttempts.outcome: failed inside the isolation before any output file existed; ruled unspent by the operator, then re-dispatched
wrote the marker, built all three files, passed the content check, then raised while assembling its result document; the runner was destroyed with the files on it
wrote the marker, built all three files in both replicas, and failed the read-back in both, byte-identically, because the read-back compared the image against the predecessor's source lock

producedOn: ubuntu-24.04-arm, the runner the predecessor producer authority sealed

producerFingerprint.what: the digests of the module, the wrapper, the workflow, the gate, the frozen helper and the read-back consumer that will run this attempt, sealed after all of them are final and before any of them runs
producerFingerprint.whyNoDigestHere: the module pins this authority's digest, so pinning the module's digest here -- directly or through a record that carries it -- would close a loop in which neither file could be written first.  The fingerprint record points at this authority; this authority names only its path.  The direction is one way on purpose.

producerPinsThatMovedElsewhere.note: The two other producer pins that no longer match the third fingerprint are declared where they moved, and are not restated here.  One file, one declaration: two records claiming the same move can disagree about it.

producerPinsThatMovedSinceTheThirdAttemp.whyItMoved: It is the file that names this authority and pins its digest, so granting a further attempt is exactly a change to these bytes.
producerPinsThatMovedSinceTheThirdAttemp.whyNoCorrectedDigestHere: the module pins this authority's digest.  Writing the module's current digest here -- even as a declaration of drift -- would close the loop this record exists to avoid, so the corrected value is recorded in the producer fingerprint, which is written after this file and points at it.

producerPinsThatMovedSinceTheThirdAttemp.declaredHereBecause: this authority binds the workflow's corrected digest, and the record that carries the other two moves was written before this change to it
producerPinsThatMovedSinceTheThirdAttemp.whyItMoved: The step that claims the preflight produced nothing now also asks the disk whether the consumed-attempt marker exists.  The claim is about the budget, and it was the one part of that claim resting on a reading of the call graph rather than on a look at the disk.

production.comparisonJobPasses: when the kernel, the initrd and the root disk are byte-identical between the two replicas.  A single differing byte is a failure of determinism, not a rounding error to be explained.

e2fsck.provesItWroteNothing: the root disk digest is retaken afterwards and must be unchanged

production.onGreen: the recorded digests are the ones both replicas reached independently.  Neither replica is picked as the winner, because picking one would turn a disagreement into a choice.

readBack.onFailure: the attempt is spent, the produced files are kept under a name and a document that disown them, and the wave stops.  A failed read-back can never yield a qualified set.
readBack.whyItIsNamedHere: The third attempt failed because this stage read the other generation's lock.  Naming the consumer and the lock in the authority means the pairing is a bound input rather than a property of whichever module the wrapper happened to call.

production.replicaIsolation: neither replica may read the other's outputs, artifacts or logs while it builds.  The comparison happens in a third job, after both have finished.
steps: rebuild the launcher on the runner and match the sealed digest
assemble the same successor staging tree the preflight assembled
produce the kernel, the initrd and the root disk
read the produced root disk back against the successor source lock, through the successor's own consumer
run e2fsck in its read-only mode exactly once against the produced root disk
publish a SHA-256 manifest of the three files

readBackCorrectionRequiredFirst.defect: the successor wrapper read its image back through the predecessor's consumer, which takes its expectations from the predecessor's source lock, so a successor image was judged against a baseline of the wrong generation
readBackCorrectionRequiredFirst.fix: a successor read-back consumer that can reach exactly one source lock -- the successor's, at the digest this authority binds -- selectable by no flag, argument, environment variable or value read out of the image, and refusing to load if its own text names the other generation's lock
readBackCorrectionRequiredFirst.why: the defect is the reason the third attempt was spent, so correcting it is a precondition of this authority rather than a follow-up to it

recordRegardlessOfVerdict: The result is written whether it passes or fails, with the same detail either way.  A failed production is evidence about the build; deleting it would make the next attempt look like the first.

forbidden: a default value for the nested tree in the successor production entry point
a fallback from the successor lock to the predecessor lock
a fallback from the predecessor lock to the successor lock
continuing when the content manifest is absent or hashes differently
requiredArguments.note: The builder keeps the nested tree optional because a projection may not change its predecessor's defaults.  The successor production path is where the argument becomes mandatory, and that is a property of the caller.

sharedMaterialization.howItIsChecked: the namespace a measurement reaches through materialize_staging_tree and the namespace a production reaches through build_oci_layout are required to be the same mapping object.  Two equal copies fail this, because two copies can drift and one object cannot.
sharedMaterialization.requirement: The production path and the measurement path must reach one function object, not two functions that agree.
sharedMaterialization.theFunction: _assemble_entries, in the fifth projection's derived namespace

subject: one production of the three arm64 boot files -- kernel, initrd and root disk -- assembled through the merge the staging measurement already took, run twice on two independent runners and required to agree byte for byte.

launcherUnit.supersededSource: native/systemd/boole-native-shadow-launcher.service stays in the tree as the predecessor path's input and is not staged into the successor image. Only the source bytes moved; the guest path is the same one.
launcherUnit.why: the host already captures and hashes the guest console.  A launcher that writes only to the journal is a launcher whose refusal the host cannot read, which is the third of the three gaps this successor closes.

nestedRuntime.replayExpectationSealsTheSameManifest: its rootfsContentManifestSha256 is the value the builder's own nested tree declaration carries, so the manifest read out of the assembled tree answers to a record sealed before the merge existed.

supersedes.note: Nothing in the superseded records is edited.  The predecessor criteria record and the three requirements it listed as not done are carried over from the third authority unchanged, because they are still closed by the same records.  The third authority still reads runsPerformed 0, which was true when it was sealed and was never updated because attempts are counted where attempts are counted: in the hard-stop records.  Its producer fingerprint still pins the bytes that produced the third attempt, and is deliberately not re-sealed over the corrected ones.

producerFingerprint.what: the bytes that produced the third attempt, so that failure stays reconstructible from the record that belongs to it

productionAuthority.what: the authority the third dispatch ran under.  It granted one attempt, the attempt was spent, and the record of that is the third hard-stop document rather than a number edited into this field.

requirementsItListedAsNotDone.how: the fourth projection widened the staging table from ten tracked files to fifteen: the five account files, and the launcher unit and tmpfiles configuration re-pointed at their v2 sources.
requirementsItListedAsNotDone.requirement: the builder stages all seven inputs

requirementsItListedAsNotDone.how: the successor plan was sealed first and the lock generated from it, in that order, so the lock is verified against the plan rather than written beside it.
requirementsItListedAsNotDone.requirement: a successor boot rootfs source lock covering the added tracked files

requirementsItListedAsNotDone.how: the fifth projection merges the nested runtime tree, and the measurement assembled it for real through that merge and walked the written tree back.  The manifest was read out of the written tree, not out of the declaration that names it.
requirementsItListedAsNotDone.requirement: the builder materialises the runtime rootfs and its manifest

theSecondAuthorityBelowThat.what: the authority the first two dispatches ran under.  It still reads runsPerformed 0, which was true when it was sealed and was never updated because the run that spent it died before it could write anything.  It is preserved with that number rather than corrected: the two hard-stop records are where the attempts are counted.

whatThisIs: The inputs, the boundaries and the pass conditions of one further successor arm64 boot image production, written down before it runs and after three prior dispatches, one unspent and two spent.  It changes the attempt identifier, the result path and the accounting, binds the corrected read-back consumer and the lock it is paired with, and carries everything else over from the authority it supersedes.  Nothing here edits any earlier authority, failure record, result, diagnosis or ruling; all of them stay byte-unchanged and are bound here by digest.
